conventions.ground_truth: main @ 2a04568 (M4-M6 merged). Every file:line below is on that commit. PR #7 = branch claude/project-thread-t6s2vg (open, not merged).
conventions.bench_class: Each answer is spliced into its own class `Bench_<model>_<qid>` (qid with '-' removed, e.g. Bench_qwen27b_T201) in a separate, never-deployed package (e.g. `EcholonBench`, listed after EcholonBot in [ModPackages]). The class extends the base_class given per question and overrides only the target.
conventions.final_functions: A `final` function cannot be overridden. For targets marked final=true the harness renames the answer to `BQ_<Name>` in the bench class (signature otherwise unchanged) so it compiles beside the original. Recursive self-calls do not occur in any chosen target.
conventions.state_targets: State functions and label code are answered by redeclaring the state in the bench class (`state X { ... }`, or `state DoObjective extends Roaming` exactly as the parent declares it) containing only the target members. UNVERIFIED: that a subclass state redeclaration with only some members compiles and inherits the rest; the harness should smoke-compile one empty redeclaration first.
conventions.consts_across_packages: UNVERIFIED: that `const` values declared in EcholonBotBase/EcholonMut are visible to subclasses in another package. Smoke-compile once; fallback is to compile the bench classes inside a throwaway copy of the EcholonBot package.
conventions.shared_prefix_coder: Coder/fixer prompts start with BIBLE_CORE.md verbatim (shared, cache-friendly), then: 'Write ONLY the target below. Output ONE ```unrealscript block containing just that function (or the state block with just the listed members). Use only symbols listed in the context or in the UE3/KF2 SDK.'
conventions.shared_prefix_review: Bug-hunter/reviewer prompts start with BIBLE_CORE.md plus the known false-alarm list from THREAD_SUMMARY_M4_M6.md (None is valid, dropped package prefixes are fine, static arrays exist, EchelonLog is the real helper name, `~=` is case-insensitive string equality).
conventions.legacy_slice: The real kit (agent_runner) also feeds the legacy KF2Bots slice via legacy_ref. Default for this benchmark: NOT included for tiers 1, 2 and 5 (contract text only, so the score measures understanding, not transcription). Each question still lists legacy_ref so the harness can switch it on.
conventions.error_lines: Tier 3 error lines below are drafts. Only "Missing '>' in 'class limitor'" is a real KFEditor message (commit dfe9f3f). Before the run, the harness compiles each injected file once and pastes the real first error line from Launch.log into the prompt.
conventions.bughunt_output: Bug-hunt answers: a JSON array of {"where": "State.Function or Function", "line": <snippet line>, "why": "one sentence"}, or [] if clean. Snippets are shown with their own line numbers 1..N; the answer key uses anchor text, which the harness maps to snippet lines.
conventions.bughunt_matching: A finding is a true positive when it names the same function, its line is within +/-2 of a key anchor line, and the 'why' names the same failure (Claude judges this blind). Findings on the neutral list score 0 either way. Everything else is a false alarm. Per bundle: precision, recall; the role score is F1 over all bundles, pooled.
conventions.review_output: Reviewer answers per diff: first line `OK` or `NOT OK`, then at most 3 lines of reason. Score: verdict correct = 1; for NOT OK items, verdict correct but reason wrong = 0.5. False 'NOT OK' on a good diff = false alarm (reported separately).
conventions.invented_names: symbols.json check: every identifier used must exist in symbols.json / contracts.json, the bench context, or sdk_symbols.json. Note ast_validator U010 checks calls only; the bench harness must also check member-variable names (swift's invented `KF` was a variable).
conventions.compile_batching: One KFEditor run per batch of answers that passed the validator; if it fails, the log names the class, that answer is marked failed and removed, recompile. Tier 3 needs one compile round per fix attempt, batched across models.
conventions.repeats: Per the plan: everything once at temp 0.6; borderline answers and the top 3 models on tiers 2 and 5 repeat twice.

grounding_notes: PR #7 read from the local clone (git fetch origin; branch claude/project-thread-t6s2vg, commits b3e6af9 and f8e6a47). GitHub MCP was not needed.
'6 real bugs' in PR #7 cover 7 code sites (HealingSelf and HealOther EndState guards are one commit bullet). All 7 sites are in the bug-hunt key.

ap's full list of 25 findings (19 false alarms) is only on the PC (kit\reports\bughunt_candidates.md), not in the repo or project files. False-alarm bait uses the categories in THREAD_SUMMARY_M4_M6.md instead. Adding the 19 real false alarms as decoys would strengthen tier 4.
The invented variable (`KF` in CheckShouldSelfHeal) is known only from commit b2ab915's message; swift's exact broken code was never committed. T3-01 and R5 re-create it.
The C4 fix landed with the initial EcholonMut import (comment at EcholonMut.uc:580); there is no separate before/after commit, so R4 is a synthetic revert.
KFEditor error messages other than "Missing '>' in 'class limitor'" are drafts; capture real ones before the run.

Unconfirmed candidate bugs noticed while drafting (in main, not in any answer key, kept out of the clean decoys): Hunting.Timer (EcholonBot.uc:1019-1061) uses the foreach variable BestZed as the 'best' result and never stores the best one; DonatingMoney.DropMoney (1674) dereferences DonateHuman after the MoneyToss Sleep without a None check; VictoryDance Begin: (1889) reads KPawn after Sleep without a None check; HealingSelf/HealOther/HealRanged Begin: wait while Physics == PHYS_Walking (1113, 1211, 1328), which looks inverted; HealRanged.EndState (1307-1309) lacks the InvManager guard PR #7 added to the other two; GoShopping Begin: uses unbounded WaitForLanding() (1561) against W4; EcholonBotLogic.RequestReroute (440) reads SquadLeader.Pawn with no None check.

EnsureSquadOrderTable (EcholonMut.uc:1349) never grew the array (THREAD_SUMMARY); the fix is only on the unpushed playtest branch, so it is not used as a question. It would make a good extra tier 2 trap once pushed.
decisions: 27 question ids: T1 x5, T2 x5, T3 x5, T4 x5 (4 bug-hunt bundles + 1 review set of 10 diffs), T5 x5, docs x2. The review set is one id but 10 scored items, to give the reviewer role weight comparable to coder.

Each known bug is used once as a bug-hunt or review item. Some functions reappear in another role (FindNearestNavPoint: T2-02 coder and R4 reviewer; CheckShouldSelfHeal: T3-01 fixer and R5 reviewer; GoShopping: T4-01 bug hunt and D-02 docs). Each prompt is sent fresh, so no answer leaks between questions.
Main already contains PR #7's bugs (PR not merged), so those bundles show main as-is; only the 3 timer bugs had to be planted back (ec120f3 reversed).
final functions are compiled as renamed BQ_<Name> copies; state targets by redeclaring the state in the bench class (both need a one-time smoke compile).
The legacy slice is off by default for coder tiers (contract text only); switch on with legacy_ref if you want the real kit prompt.
T2-04 asks for a None re-check after latent waits that the merged reference lacks; scored as a bonus point so swift's reference doesn't define the ceiling.
Bug-hunt answers use anchor text rather than file line numbers so plants that shift lines don't break the key.
Reasoning budgets per tier: T1 2k, T2 4k, T3 2k, T4 4k, T5 8k, docs 2k (from the plan).

context: one diff per call (10 calls), plus the full containing function after the change

--- a/Classes/EcholonMut.uc  (function MoveSquadMembers)
+++ b/Classes/EcholonMut.uc
